characterList.name: Leland Sklar

content_metadata.description: A spontaneous encounter and conversation capturing Leland Sklar's personality and experiences.

qAndA.answer: It serves as a humorous anecdote, highlighting the relaxed and casual atmosphere of the event.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of Jason's missing wristband?

qAndA.answer: He emphasizes practicality and accessibility, believing that good music can be created with standard equipment.
qAndA.question: Why does Leland prefer off-the-shelf instruments?

qAndA.answer: He received a last-minute call because Mike Porcaro's illness prevented him from touring.
qAndA.question: How did Leland Sklar join Toto for their Falling in Between Live DVD?

qAndA.answer: He uses mandolin fret wire, the thinnest type available, for a specific playing feel.
qAndA.question: What kind of fret wire does Leland use on his basses?

qAndA.answer: He lends them to young musicians to encourage their passion for music, often giving them away if the student shows dedication.
qAndA.question: What does Leland do with instruments he doesn't use regularly?

youtube_description:
Another of my interviews from NAMM 2015. Don't be surprised if you've seen Leland Sklar at a show you've been to before or at least on a DVD or YouTube concert video. He's everywhere. Phil Collins, Rod Stuart, Jackson Brown, Kim Carnes, Dolly Parton, Crosby & Nash (& Stills) (& Young), Linda Ronstadt, James Taylor, Lisa Loeb and this list just goes on & on. A remarkable musician & a remarkable man with amazing character.

NOTE: I no longer work for Ishibashi Music. This video is only here for historical and entertainment purposes.

For more on Leland & his Warwick Basses follow this link to the Artist page and then scroll around half way down to find him. It's well worth a look.
http://www.warwickbass.com/en/Warwick---Artists--Artist.html

www.facebook.com/JasonVideoMusicTokyo

Audio recorder: Zoom H6
#JasonVideoMusicTokyo
